text: The actions jsonb of an agent-step decision entry carries the agent run id, the autonomy mode, the fallback flag and its reason, and the entry carries the agent version as a string of the form AGENT@POLICY/PROMPT and the model version as a separate value, with no new column of decision_log_entry; the decision code of an agent step is read as a value of LOV-DECISION and the fixtures carry D6, the route decision an agent step of the route agent sits in; the two reads answer the field set TSD P7 v2 T3.1 names plus the actions members of the entry, and the ledger record on rwb.decision-record.v1 carries the four fields of EV-08 plus the agent and model versions, the inputs reference, the recommendation, the final call, the actions, the decided time and the idempotency key.
why: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 has no column for a run id, a mode or a reason, its actions is the only jsonb, T3.2 does not enumerate LOV-DECISION, and T-A.2 gives no answer field set; inventing a column or a sub-decision code would put a value into the build that no owner approved.
read: TSD P7 v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.2; FSD P7 v3 A2.1.4.2 AC-ALT-P7-001-02; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-08; Architecture v5 slides 17 and 41; legacy RWB-TE-013 sections 4 and 12
applied_in: RWB-P7-TE013-APP sections 1, 4, 7 (AC1, AC2, AC4, AC8), 11, 12.1 and 12.4
confirm: Solution architect, with the P10 business analyst and the data steward, at the wave 1 design review and in the OpenAPI of the service
impact: The entry and the two reads are built against the assumed shape; a later contract revision renames members without a change of behaviour, because the agent facts stay P10's and are only referenced here

text: The agent fallback rate is a measure of rwb-reporting and not of this story: the ledger only guarantees that the agent version is on every entry that had one and that the fallback fact and its reason are in its actions, so the measure can be defined from the entries; no measure name, target or window is written in the story and none is a constant of the code.
why: Architecture v5 slide 41 gives P9 the measures and slide 28 the measure publish, the legacy target is a business value with no parameter row, and writing either into this service would put a measure in the wrong owner's code.
read: Legacy RWB-TE-013 section 2; Architecture v5 slides 28 and 41; FSD P7 v3 A2.1; TSD P7 v2 T-A.1; Template and Rules v1 R3 and R5.5 DP-06
confirm: Data steward with the P9 reporting analyst, at the measures review
impact: The measure is defined without a change to the ledger; if a target or a window is needed it is a parameter row of rwb-case and not a release

text: A record the ingest refuses is answered with MSG-P7-009 naming the field that failed, is held for the retry and dead-letter path with an alert, and adds nothing to the ledger and nothing to the chain; the message text is a catalogue value and the story writes no wording of its own.
why: FSD P7 v3 names MSG-P7-009 without its text and no source fixes the refusal treatment; the safe reading is the one the platform inbox and dead-letter pattern already gives every consumer, and it keeps the ledger append-only and gap-free.
read: FSD P7 v3 A2.2.4.2 and A2.2.4.3; TSD P7 v2 T-A.2; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 20; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09; legacy RWB-TE-013 section 5
confirm: Solution architect with the platform event team, at the topic contract review
impact: The failure path is buildable now; a later wording of MSG-P7-009 changes the catalogue and not the behaviour

text: The database login of the capability is the per-service login of DP-02 and the story calls it the rwb-decision login (DP-02); no login name is written in the story, a migration or a test, and the shared login of the monolith is never named.
why: Architecture v5 gives every service its own login but no source fixes the name of this one, and a guessed name would become a credential in a script.

confirm: ACE DB team at the schema and login allocation of wave 1
impact: One identifier in the migration and the deployment values; nothing else depends on it

text: The seven platform H dependencies, the three published C dependencies and the P4 authorise answer that the pattern table adds are read as DP-added and carried outside the metadata rows; every H is a platform CON story and every C is built against its published contract and fake, so Ready to start stays Day 1 and no lane changes.
why: R5.4 lets an APP story build against published contracts and their fakes, and R5.7 rule 8 keeps Day 1 when the only H dependencies are platform CON stories; the metadata rows are copied from the plan and must not be altered.

text: The model version of agent INTAKE is a P10 fact that arrives inside the record; the fixtures of this story carry a synthetic model version and the criteria assert that the value is present and travels unchanged, never a particular value.
why: The legacy story names a model version only for another agent, and a model version is an approved P10 fact; asserting a value here would invent it.
read: Legacy RWB-TE-013 sections 3 and 7; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3; Architecture v5 slide 41
confirm: P10 agent runtime business analyst with the model risk officer, at the agent policy approval
impact: The ledger is model-version agnostic; a change of model is a policy change and not a change of this story

text: A record whose append fails is not chained and leaves the ledger unchanged: the ingest answers MSG-P7-009 with the failing field, holds the record for the retry and dead-letter path with an alert, and the calling step does not act, because the record must be written before the action; the retry is idempotent on the step key, so a second attempt finds the first entry or appends exactly one.
why: The append-only chain must have no gap and the legacy story already makes the decision record a precondition of the action (MSG-P7-003, R-UNI-39); no source writes the refusal shape, so it is read from the platform inbox and dead-letter pattern.
